analysis:
Examined both complete BASE/HEAD files, lifecycle patch and mode metadata against the canonical definition index and supplied T-041 detail. No independently supported security regression is established in this source scope.

ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift:82 adds awaited selected-model recovery to the periodic capacity tick, after inventory registration and before daemon-state writing. Existing memory/reservation accounting, stale-snapshot guards, nonroutable drain/fault states, cache-evidence publication and heartbeat throttling are unchanged. Integration must examine checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue: its implementation is absent here. Verify bounded/cancellable recovery, lifecycle/drain ownership, load admission and model-identity verification, and whether recovery preserves cache build/scope bindings (TB-007, T-012, T-027, T-029, T-041).

ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift:105-125 now allows an empty disconnected session to finish draining without coordinator acknowledgement, after up to ten seconds of reconnect grace. Admission closure, local/coordinator work counts, native-owner retirement and App Attest worker retirement remain required; coordinatorAcknowledged remains false when bypassed. Shutdown callers at 190-213 retain native/worker retirement checks. This does not visibly grant trust, weaken encryption or assert remote credential revocation.

Material integration contract: verify hasRegisteredConnection, acknowledgeDrain and disconnect handling actually cancel/fence accepted work, discard outbound traffic and retire the old connection's authorization; confirm a reconnect during worker retirement cannot admit new work or deliver stale terminal/usage messages. The comment at lifecycle lines 100-102 is not implementation evidence. These contracts affect cancellation, usage ordering and connection-bound authorization (TB-002, TB-011, T-010, T-053). Also reconcile selected-model recovery with lifecycle-owned admission closure. Missing implementations are coverage limits, not findings.
